prerequisites: A solid background in secondary school algebra and trigonometry.
Students are advised to attend the mathematics pre-courses offered in the two weeks prior to the start of the courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will compute, analyze, and communicate quantitative data using mathematical and logical methods to solve problems.

syllabus_topics: Sets, binary relations, functions or mappings
Equivalence relations and partitions of a set
Binary operations, groups, fields, and real vector spaces
Subspaces of vector spaces
Spanning sets and linear indipendence
Basis and dimension
Vectors in R^n
Matrices
Operations with matrices and their properties
Rank of a matrix and its properties
The determinant of a matrix and its properties
Evaluate determinants using elementary operations
The inverse of a matrix
Introduction to system of linear equations
Application of Gauss-Jordan method to system of linear equations
Introduction of eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Matrix diagonalization
Introduction to the analytical geometry of space: lines and planes
Conics (quadratic curves) in the plane
Euclidean and afine classification of quadratic curves
The sphere, the cone and the cylinder
teaching_methods: Distance learning (in case of health emergency)
assessment_rules: The Geometry exam consists of two tests. The first test (written) assesses exercise-solving ability, and passing it is necessary to participate in the second test. The second test (oral or written) assesses knowledge of basic notions and ability to prove theorems. The commission decides if the student has passed and proposes a grade, taking both tests into account. Students can accept the grade, refuse it (losing both tests and needing to retake them), or ask for Lauds if the grade is 30/30 (if they fail this question, the mark remains 30/30).
